annotations.text:
Three directions for the home page: hero + Selected work. Same palette, fonts, copy and figures as the live site; what changes is composition and motion. Pick one and I build it into the Next.js site.
Each note below says how it moves on scroll, and what it costs.

A · DEPTH STAGE — the photo-led, cinematic one.
Motion: three planes on scroll. The huge name in the background drifts at 0.2x, the fleet orbit and photo at 0.6x, the copy at 1x; the orbit dots pulse as events fire. Work is a horizontal strip: the focused card is full-size, the next ones step back and dim; scroll (or drag) advances one card at a time and the dots track position.
Why: closest to the Astra demos, the most 'wow' on first load.
Cost: the horizontal strip fights the vertical read on phones (it collapses to a stack there), and the big background name needs care at narrow widths.

B · EDITORIAL LEDGER — the typography-led one.
Motion: the two-line headline settles in word by word; the ledger rows reveal one at a time as they cross mid-screen, the active row's number turns green and its accent line draws across; the big figures count up once, then stay.
Why: reads like a magazine feature, calm and confident, and it is the most honest to the 'every number says how it was measured' voice. Cheapest to build and the best on phones.
Cost: the least visual spectacle; the photo is small; someone skimming for a demo feel may find it plain.

C · DATA COCKPIT — the dense, terminal one.
Motion: the cockpit panel boots on load (a scan line, tiles filling in, the trace ticking) and stays sticky while the tiles below rise in one by one; hovering a tile lifts it and lights its figure. This is the current site's terminal flavour pushed further.
Why: says 'production systems' at a glance; every headline figure is above the fold.
Cost: the busiest of the three; risk of reading as a dashboard rather than a person. Bento tiles need real content in every cell or they look empty.
